key_insight: The authors discover a Latent Color Subspace (LCS) in the VAE latent space of FLUX that organizes color along separable Hue, Saturation, and Lightness directions, enabling predictable, controlled color changes via simple linear operations in latent space.
problem_solved: Text-to-image models lack interpretable, fine-grained control over color. This work identifies how color is encoded internally and provides a mechanism to predict and manipulate it reliably.
method: Analyze latent representations from the FLUX VAE with image color annotations to find structure correlating with H, S, L.
Use dimensionality reduction and linear probes (e.g., PCA/linear regression) to identify an orthogonal subspace capturing color axes.
Validate the Latent Color Subspace by predicting color attributes and performing latent-space interventions to reproduce controlled H/S/L changes in reconstructions.
impact: Provides a simple, interpretable handle for color editing and diagnostics in generative models, improving controllability and explainability for practitioners working on image synthesis and editing.
visual_elements: 2D/3D latent scatter colored by Hue, with clear gradients showing H/S/L alignment
Diagram of latent vector decomposition showing orthogonal H, S, L axes and a sample vector projection
Before/after image triplets demonstrating latent interventions that alter Hue, Saturation, or Lightness independently
Schematic pipeline: input image -> encoder -> LCS probe -> modified latent -> decoder -> edited image
paper_title: The Latent Color Subspace: Emergent Order in High-Dimensional Chaos
paper_authors: Mateusz Pach, Jessica Bader, Quentin Bouniot, Serge Belongie, Zeynep Akata
